text:
Maya: Quick decision point: we need a measurement plan for the pilot SLA (how we compute p95/p99, what traffic counts, sampling, and credit calc) before we lock consent language.
Priya: Recommendation: compute p95/p99 over successful inference latencies only (HTTP 200). Count only requests that hit the model, exclude warmup/probe calls. Use sliding 15m windows for alerting, 30d windows for monthly SLA calculation.
Jon: Agree on excluding probes, but we should include 4xx client errors in billing and expose them separately. For SLO math, include only 5xx+ timeout errors as failures.
Arjun: Note: KV cache hits massively change latency distributions. Suggest we report SLOs both "raw" (observed) and "cache-normalized" where we strip cache-hit latency to show model-only tail. Customers asked for both.
Liam: For credits: Finance prefers simple formula. My draft: If monthly p99 > SLA p99 then credit = min(20% * monthly usage, (observed_p99 - sla_p99)/sla_p99 * 100% * monthly usage). Cap at committed amount. Need legal review.
Elena: Legal: prefer deterministic calculation. Suggest credits = (overage_fraction) * monthly invoice where overage_fraction = max(0, (observed_p99 - sla_p99)/observed_p99). Also require an SLA window of a full calendar month to compute credits and explicit exclusions (maintenance, force majeure, customer's infra).
Maya: We also must state which endpoints and model variants are covered. Hosted redwood-managed models = covered; dedicated reserved nodes = covered under Dedicated contract; private on-prem = not covered (customer-managed).
Jon: Telemetry tagging: include fields: model_id, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, route, region, cache_hit (true/false), reserved_node_id (if any), billing_tag. That allows slicing.
Priya: We'll need to surface examples in the FAQ: "How are long inputs measured?" Answer: seq_len bucket tag controls SLA applicability. If seq_len > 1024, request marked as 'long' and excluded from latency SLA but billed normally.
Arjun: For alerting, propose two streams: urgent (p99 breach or error spike) -> PD page; and ops-info (p95 drift) -> #eng-oncall. Auto-ticket creation for urgent events with runbook link.
ops-bot: Note: runbook template added: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/pilot-measurement-and-credits. Fill "Measurement" and "Credit-calc" sections.
Liam: Pricing interplay: if fallback quantized model is used during rollback, we should bill based on the variant actually served. Make sure billing exports include model_variant and quantization_tag.
Elena: Legal: include explicit customer opt-in checkbox stating: "I accept Pilot SLA: limited latency guarantees per seq_len buckets, credits per monthly window, and exclusions." We also need consent for telemetry sharing for SLA validation.
Priya: On sampling: to reduce noise, we'll sample at 100% for pilot customers. For GA, allow adaptive sampling but still compute SLA on full set of qualifying requests in billing window.
Jon: Multi-region nuance: SLA should be region-specific. If a customer's traffic is split across regions, compute per-region SLOs and aggregate only if customer purchased global SLA. Add that variant to doc.
Arjun: Edge-case: retries. Do we count retries as separate requests for SLA? I suggest count only the final successful attempt for latency percentile, but count errors for error-rate SLO.
Maya: Good catch. Add that to measurement rules.
Liam: For credits, finance also wants a one-time manual review trigger if credits calculation exceeds 10% of invoice, to avoid systemic measurement bugs.
Elena: We'll add a clause: large credit triggers manual review and possible delay in credit issuance pending audit.
Priya: Monitoring slices we need in dashboards: p95/p99 by seq_len_bucket, cache_hit ratio, per-model p99, reserved_node utilization, error-rate per code bucket, and percent of traffic excluded from SLA (long-context).
Jon: Devex needs a small API snippet in docs showing how customers can tag requests for billing and how to query their per-model SLA telemetry. I'll draft that.
Maya: Ownership: Priya owns the measurement doc + FAQ. Arjun owns tagging + runbook updates. Liam owns credit formula draft and billing export spec. Elena & legal-bot to sign off on consent text. Jon handles devex snippets and example queries. I'll review and sign-off.
ops-bot: Action: create release-war-room ticket after measurement doc is uploaded.
legal-bot: Reminder: include sample legal text for opt-in and a clear list of exclusions.
Maya: Timeline: measurement + consent draft by EOD, billing export spec by COB tomorrow, runbook and dashboards ready before pilot start.
Jon: One more: add a small note in docs about how on-prem/private deployments may have different SLA measurement since telemetry might not be forwarded.
Priya: Will do.
Maya: Thanks team. Locking decisions unless major objections. :thumbsup:
